keys.undoNotice: The last import or reset can be undone after an IITC refresh. A new import or reset replaces that backup. Direct manual changes do not create a backup.

keys.noUndo: No saved key change to undo.
keys.undoReview: Restore the counts before the last import or reset. Later changes are marked as conflicts and are not selected. Select a conflict only if you want to overwrite its current count. Unselected conflicts remain available for later undo.
keys.listNotice: Complete inventory from IITC Keys, including portals outside the plan. Names come from the plan, loaded portals or bookmarks; unavailable names remain marked. This list does not change inventory.
keys.usageNotice: A plan link previously seen as open uses one key at its confirmed target when it is newly detected in Intel. Existing links at the first scan are not charged. Repeated scans or refreshes do not charge the same link twice. Links built by other players also trigger this rule.
keys.usageStorage: Automatic key consumption could not be saved safely. No further automatic booking for this observation; check browser storage and inventory.
keys.usageCheck: Check key inventory: automatic consumption was unavailable or interrupted. Confirm the direction and correct/import the current count before marking it checked.
walk.title: 計画プレビュー
walk.notice: Preview of the remaining work route. Required portal captures/claims are explicit virtual actions before dependent links, based on observed ownership. Unknown ownership remains unresolved and blocks simulated throws. Removing a blocker does not capture its other endpoint. Real portals, inventory and completion stay unchanged. Existing friendly portals are assumed link-ready; deployment resources, link limits, range and linking under fields still need checking. Triangles remain geometric previews, not guaranteed fields. Close and reopen after a plan change. Purple shows the target, orange travel, cyan simulated building.

fan.title: Fan planner
fan.help: First draw a Draw Tools polygon around the desired portals. The fan planner evaluates loaded portals inside it. Select the desired polygon if there are several. Each fan portal belongs to one anchor; manual anchors (★) remain pinned. Proposals are drawn directly. Use plan activates the native plan for tasks and routing; the anchor-portal plan is preserved. Direction suggestions in Tasks consider available keys but remain unconfirmed. Geometric field counts do not guarantee build order.
fan.summary: {anchors} anchors · {links} links · {fields} geometric fields · {blocked} blocked plan links · {existing} plan links counted as existing
fan.limit: Select 3–200 portals. Reduce the polygon or exclude portals for larger selections.
fan.invalid: Duplicate portals, coincident positions or missing coordinates. Review the selection.
fan.anchorsNeeded: Select at least one anchor and leave at least one fan portal.
fan.invalidAssignment: A manually assigned anchor is missing. Review assignments.
fan.conflict: Assigned fans contain crossing or overlapping radial links. Change anchors or assignments.
fan.noFields: No non-degenerate fields are possible with this selection.
fan.busy: Close Plan preview or pause Final check before designing/applying fans.
fan.applyFailed: Could not save the fan plan. The previous plan is preserved.
fan.areaRequired: First draw a simple selection polygon with Draw Tools, then load portals. Polygons with holes are unsupported.

ui.fanHelp: Design and execute a native fan plan from a selection polygon.
ui.fanEmpty: Design a new fan from the current selection polygon. Previous plans, anchors and assignments are not reused. You can explicitly open a saved fan separately.
ui.settingsHelp: These settings apply to the whole plugin. Clear data removes the saved fan plan and portal/link settings. Draw Tools drawings and inventory in the Keys plugin are preserved.
ui.fanScanHelp: Refresh the accepted fan plan to review its portals and tasks.

spine.title: Spine fields · two anchors
spine.help: Draft: select exactly two anchors, manually or with Suggest anchors. The planner finds a nested portal chain on one side of their baseline. Each spine portal links to both anchors and, after the first, its predecessor. Unsuitable portals stay out of the accepted plan. Preview first; directions remain unconfirmed. Field count is a geometric target, not a guaranteed build or AP estimate.
spine.twoAnchors: Spine fields require exactly two anchors. Set the count to 2 and keep at most two manually fixed anchors.
spine.noChain: No suitable spine found for this anchor pair. Choose different anchors or portals.
spine.summary: {count} spine portals · {unused} unsuitable portals omitted. One side of the baseline; anchor-pair suggestions use a bounded search.
spine.routeOrder: Spine build order · travel respects throw sequence
spine.workflow: Spine build order: baseline first; then each spine portal to both anchors and its predecessor. Confirm directions individually. A different route origin preserves construction order. Existing links can change the field outcome.
spine.prerequisite: Earlier spine throws are still missing
spine.countHelp: Choose exactly two anchors for this draft. Manually fixed anchors (★) stay fixed; release any extra anchors first.
